API availability is not redistribution permission.
Institutional or repository status does not automatically authorize public PDF redistribution.
Item-level license/terms must be captured before public release.
No source in this registry is treated as an AI translation source.

sources.notes: Interim catalogue covering Oriental Manuscripts and Endangered Archives material; not all items are digitized or currently available.

sources.name: Malay World Manuscript Research Centre (PPMAM)
sources.notes: UKM research centre for Malay Jawi manuscripts; documents a worldwide research scope and manuscript holdings in libraries, archives and museums.

sources.name: UKM Learning and Research Repository — Manuscripts Collection
sources.notes: 78-item manuscript collection; catalogue includes religious works such as Tajwid, Hadith and Hanafi fiqh; file access varies by item.

sources.name: Osoul Global Center
sources.notes: Official Osoul site; multilingual dawah materials. Item-level license/redistribution terms must be verified before acquisition.

sources.name: Comprehensive Muslim e-Library (EDC)
sources.notes: EDC/Al-Najat library; free downloadable PDF catalog in many languages. Item-level rights must be verified before redistribution.

sources.name: Conveying Islamic Message Society (CIMS)
sources.notes: Egyptian non-profit society distributing Islamic books and pamphlets in multiple languages. Item-level rights must be verified.

sources.name: Zad Group
sources.notes: Saudi technology/media/publishing group with digital education and content services. No blanket open-license assumption.

sources.name: Mawthuq Islamic Content Archive
sources.notes: Provides JSON API access to content from multiple Islamic sites; API access is not itself redistribution permission.

sources.name: KFGQPC Developer Resources
sources.notes: Official King Fahd Complex developer/resource page. Specific datasets and translations require item-level rights verification.

sources.name: Islamic Content Association / IslamContent
sources.notes: Official Islamic Content Association site. Registered already as a distinct organization/source from the IslamContent content platform; its existence does not grant redistribution rights, and item-level terms remain required.

sources.name: Tafsir Center for Quranic Studies
sources.notes: Official Tafsir Center applications/resources, including Quran applications. API/data rights must be verified per resource.

sources.name: Alminasa.ai — المنصة الحديثية
sources.notes: Official platform for hadith research; official site and app materials describe interactive/semantic search, hadith-path visualization, narrator information, explanations and hadith grading tools. AI-assisted features are treated as research/indexing signals, not as independent scholarly evidence.

sources.name: Hdith.com — الموسوعة الحديثية
sources.notes: Digital hadith encyclopedia with structured hadith pages, isnad/narrator information, takhrij and scholar judgments visible on indexed pages. Content/licensing and bulk-access terms require item-level verification before redistribution.

sources.name: King Salman Complex for the Noble Prophetic Hadith
sources.notes: Official institutional source. Saudi regulations state the Complex serves hadith through collection, classification, verification, study and publication, including multilingual publication and use of modern technologies. Do not assume open/copy-left redistribution without explicit terms.

sources.name: Mubseroon — جمعية العوق البصري الأهلية ببريدة
sources.notes: Official Saudi association serving people with visual disabilities; its site documents Braille-related tools and a Braille learning platform. The stronger claims about a 45-language Islamic Open-API infrastructure were not independently verified, so they are not encoded as facts.

sources.name: HadithWeb — جامع خادم الحرمين الشريفين للسنة النبوية المطهرة
sources.notes: Officially documented hadith research program presented by the General Presidency for Scholarly Research and Ifta in cooperation with Harf Information Technology. The official description documents 33 core hadith books, 57 supporting works, hadith takhrij, narrator biographies exceeding 18,800 narrators, and other research services. Redistribution/API terms must be verified before acquisition.

sources.name: UmmahAPI
sources.notes: Public Islamic REST API covering Quran, hadith, tafsir, duas and other services. Official documentation states JSON REST endpoints and currently lists 36,000+ hadith from 10 collections and 12 Quran translations. API availability does not by itself grant redistribution rights for underlying source texts.

sources.name: Dua & Ruqyah — mrhrifat/dua-ruqyah
sources.notes: Public GitHub repository for a Dua/Ruqyah web app using Quran and hadith references, categories, translations and references. Repository is GPL-3.0, but the license applies to the code and does not automatically relicense third-party religious source data.

sources.name: Saudi Digital Library (SDL)
sources.notes: Candidate institutional academic-library source. Access, bulk acquisition, multilingual availability and redistribution rights must be verified per item/provider; no blanket public-domain claim is asserted.

sources.name: Islamic University of Madinah Digital Library
sources.notes: Official university domain used as an institutional discovery source. Specific digital-library endpoints and item-level rights require verification before acquisition.

sources.name: Umm Al-Qura University
sources.notes: Official university domain used as an institutional discovery source. Specific library/repository endpoints and item-level rights require verification before acquisition.

sources.name: Imam Mohammad Ibn Saud Islamic University
sources.notes: Official university domain used as an institutional discovery source. Specific repository/library endpoints and item-level rights require verification before acquisition.

sources.name: Tadween Center for Hadith Research and Studies — مركز تدوين
sources.notes: Official Tadween Center site; identifies the center as a non-profit endowment registered in Saudi Arabia and lists databases for theses, peer-reviewed research, manuscripts, Sunnah works and hadith terminology. Item/API access and redistribution rights require verification.

sources.name: Al-Furqan Islamic Heritage Foundation Digital Library
sources.notes: Official Al-Furqan Digital Library gateway. Its collections include manuscripts, World Collections, Maqasid, library references and publications; the platform documents Islamic manuscript and bibliographic records across many countries and languages. It is a discovery/research gateway, not blanket authorization for PDF redistribution; rights must be verified per item.

sources.name: The New Muslim Guide
sources.notes: Official site states the guide was revised and approved by a number of Muslim scholars and translated into 26 languages. The project identifies itself as The New Muslim Guide/Modern Guide; item-level rights are reserved and must be verified before redistribution.

sources.name: Ilmverse
sources.notes: Official site states its library covers Quran/Tafsir, hadith, fiqh in all four schools, Seerah and more, with source-linked answers and scholar testing. Treat AI outputs as indexing/research assistance only; underlying-source rights and bulk access require verification.

sources.name: IslamLand
sources.notes: Official site states that it introduces Islam in more than 140 languages and contains thousands of books, videos and audios. Indexed book pages expose PDF/Word downloads for multiple language paths. Item-level redistribution rights must still be verified.

sources.name: Osoulstore
sources.notes: Official Osoul bookstore states 704 books in 56 languages, including 611 PDF books, and lists languages spanning African, Asian, European and other language families. Item-level licensing/redistribution terms must be checked before release.

sources.name: Explore Islam
sources.notes: Official Explore Islam pages expose downloadable ebooks in multiple languages; indexed examples include Romanian and English, and site materials document multilingual Islamic books/media. Underlying item rights must be verified before redistribution.

sources.name: Weg zum Islam
sources.notes: German-language Sunni-oriented discovery source; its official about page describes Quran, Sunnah, hadith, books and free downloads. It is useful for German-language matrix cells, but it is not itself a multilingual source, so it is recorded as a language-specific lane rather than a global multilingual provider.

sources.name: Australian Islamic Library
sources.notes: Site provides Hadith books in multiple languages and dedicated world-languages, fiqh, aqeedah and fatawa sections. Individual download/copyright terms must be verified before redistribution.

sources.name: Hadith Hub GO
sources.notes: Official site states 12 hadith collections and 9 languages, with the full text held offline. Treat as a discovery/structured-data source; redistribution rights for translations/data require verification.

sources.name: Al-Hadith Bibliothèque Islam
sources.notes: Current app listing states 12 hadith collections, 50,000+ hadith and translations in 9 languages. Source/data licensing and bulk extraction must be verified before acquisition.

sources.name: Hadith Tabsera
sources.notes: Official site presents Arabic narrations with English and Somali translations and scholarly explanations; open-access claim is site-level and does not by itself settle redistribution of every underlying translation.

sources.name: Islamtics Hadith Library
sources.notes: Current hadith pages expose Sahih al-Bukhari in 10 languages. Use as a discovery/reference lane; verify translation provenance and redistribution rights before downloading into public storage.

sources.category: Multilingual Quran API and downloadable data
sources.name: GlobalQuran.com
sources.notes: Official documentation describes REST APIs and downloadable Quran resources; the project documentation also describes 100+ language translations and bulk downloads. Verify each translation's upstream license before redistribution.

sources.name: Wathakker
sources.notes: Current indexed editions identify Wathakker as publisher and expose PDF/Word downloads on multilingual IslamLand mirrors. Treat the Wathakker imprint and each edition's rights separately; do not infer blanket redistribution permission.

sources.name: AlQuranTranslation.com
sources.notes: Current site provides Quran translations and downloadable PDF/text/MP3/RAR packages in 120+ languages. Treat it as an acquisition/discovery source until translator/publisher rights are verified per edition.

sources.name: Quran Mercy
sources.notes: Current site exposes Quran translation downloads in 120+ languages and multilingual Islamic pamphlets. It may overlap materially with other multilingual translation mirrors; SHA-256 deduplication must prevent duplicate acquisition.

sources.name: UrduPoint Islamic Books
sources.notes: Current Islamic-book index lists major hadith works and Islamic books in multiple South Asian languages. Rights and edition provenance must be verified per downloadable item.

sources.name: HolyBooks.in
sources.notes: Current site advertises Islamic PDFs across multiple languages and categories. It is an aggregator rather than a blanket rights authority; source/publisher/license must be captured for every acquired item.

sources.category: Islamic source discovery and scholarly indexing
sources.name: Nuria
sources.notes: Current site describes Quran, hadith and source-citing Islamic knowledge interfaces. AI responses must remain indexing/retrieval assistance only; underlying cited sources require independent verification before entering the scholarly corpus or download workflow.

sources.name: Download Islamic Religion PDF Ebooks
sources.notes: Current sitemap explicitly lists an Islamic-books section with PDF downloads and a separate 'Islamic Books in Other Languages' section with 23 language categories. The catalog contains mixed material, so Sunni/madhhab and edition provenance filtering plus item-level rights review are mandatory.

sources.name: Bayyinah TV
languages: Urdu support documented; additional subtitle languages require item verification
sources.notes: Official language/subtitle support documentation confirms multilingual subtitle capability. Primarily audiovisual educational content; acquire transcripts/subtitles only where rights and permitted formats allow.

sources.name: AccessibleQuran
sources.notes: The current App Store listing documents VoiceOver accessibility and states Quran text/translations come from the Quran.com API and audio from EveryAyah. It is an accessibility client, not itself a rights authority for underlying translations/audio.

sources.name: Islamic Library Data
sources.notes: Public GitHub repository contains structured JSON datasets for Quran, Hadith, Azkar, Duas, Prophet Stories, Names of Allah and Tafsir, served via jsDelivr. Underlying text provenance/licensing must be audited per dataset before corpus or redistribution use.

sources.name: Islamic API by SolimanAnas
sources.notes: Public GitHub project documents REST endpoints for Quran, 13 hadith collections, Hisn Muslim, Tafsir and audio. Treat API availability as a technical access signal, not a redistribution license for every underlying work.

sources.name: Tebian Academy
sources.notes: Current official site documents Quran recitation/Tajweed, Tafsir and Quranic sciences, Arabic, Fiqh, Seerah and Hadith sciences. Site UI is available in Arabic, English, French and Italian. It is an educational provider, not a bulk-PDF repository; content rights require item-level review.

sources.name: Nawara Academy
sources.notes: Current site states that its structured courses are free and span Aqeedah, Quran/Tafsir, Arabic/Quran reading, Seerah, Fiqh, Hadith sciences and other fields. It curates publicly available YouTube lessons from original teachers/institutions; the original channel remains the rights holder, so it is a discovery source rather than a blanket redistribution license.

sources.category: Islamic and Arabic manuscript digital library
sources.name: Cambridge University Digital Library (CUDL)
sources.notes: CUDL is a distinct digital-library gateway for Cambridge collections and currently exposes digitized Muhammadan/Islamic manuscript catalogues and folio/transcription records. Individual manuscript image/download rights must be checked at item level; the library gateway itself is not a blanket redistribution license.

sources.category: Arabic and Islamic books publisher / multilingual publications
sources.name: Noon Books
sources.notes: Current publisher site identifies Noon Books as the Nahed Al-Shawa Cultural Foundation, with books distributed in 50+ countries and translated into 7+ languages. Its Islamic collection includes contemporary titles such as creed books and prophet stories. It is a publisher/catalogue rather than a free PDF repository; acquisition requires item-level permission or applicable license.

sources.name: Arab Union Catalog (AUC)
sources.notes: Official site currently exposes the bibliographic database, digital-library collections and country/library portals, and reports 4.2 million bibliographic/authority records, 500 knowledge institutions and 4,512 central/subsidiary libraries across 25 countries. It is a discovery/catalogue source, not itself a blanket PDF download source.

sources.name: IslamicManuscripts.info
sources.notes: The supplied domain is no longer reliably live; current web evidence preserves references to its manuscript reference library and materials, including Islamic codicology/palaeography resources. Registered as a legacy discovery/archival pointer only—not as an active acquisition endpoint. Prefer the surviving institutional catalogues and archive copies for actual acquisition.

sources.name: Digital Library of the Middle East (DLME)
sources.notes: The supplied MED Dialogue page describes DLME as a federated platform for archives, manuscripts, museum objects, media and archaeological/intangible heritage, with records from the Middle East and North Africa. It is a discovery/aggregation layer; item-level rights and provider links must be followed before acquisition.

sources.name: Bibliothèques d'Orient (Libraries of the Middle East)
sources.notes: BnF describes Bibliothèques d'Orient as a collaborative curated digital library covering the Arab East and Turkish/Persian worlds. The current French institutional page reports more than 10,000 documents and identifies partner institutions in Egypt, Lebanon, Jerusalem, Istanbul, Erbil and elsewhere. Item-level rights vary by contributing institution.

sources.category: MENA manuscript discovery and library guide
sources.name: University of Illinois MENA Manuscripts Guide
sources.notes: The exact supplied URL is a University of Illinois research guide. It states that its linked digital collections are free and open access and aggregates access points for Arabic/West African, Mali, Princeton, Michigan, Wellcome and other manuscript collections. It is a discovery hub rather than the underlying item host.

sources.name: Princeton Digital Library of Islamic Manuscripts
sources.notes: Added separately because the user's description names Princeton but the supplied URL actually points to the University of Illinois guide. Princeton's current digital collection reports 3,456 items and 7 languages; individual items may expose image files and PDF download options. Rights are determined at item level.

sources.category: Arabic and Islamic manuscripts digital collection
sources.name: University of Manchester — Arabic Manuscripts
sources.notes: John Rylands collection has nearly 900 Arabic codices spanning about 1,000 years; the current digital collection emphasizes Quranic manuscripts and other Islamic works.

sources.category: Asian and Islamic manuscript digital collections
sources.name: Royal Asiatic Society Online Manuscripts
sources.notes: RAS reports around 2,000 manuscripts from across Asia, with a growing digitized portion; its collections include Persian, Malay, Arabic-script, Urdu and other Asian manuscript traditions.

sources.category: Islamic and world manuscript museum collection
sources.name: Chester Beatty — Digitised Collections
sources.notes: The museum states that its holdings cover more than 25,000 objects in over 50 languages, with an Islamic curatorial division and an online image database. Item-level rights apply.

sources.name: National Library of Israel — Warraq
sources.notes: The Warraq project digitized nearly 2,500 Islamic manuscripts in high resolution and states that users can search, read, download and share them free of charge. Record-level rights/metadata should still be preserved.

sources.name: Diyanet Quran Library
sources.notes: Official Turkish Directorate of Religious Affairs Quran portal includes a library, tafsir thesis archive and links to Quran resources. Useful for Turkish-language Quran/Islamic materials; reuse rights require item-level review.

sources.category: Turkish Islamic books and digitized publications
sources.name: Diyanet Digital Library
sources.notes: Official Diyanet digital library currently exposes Turkish Islamic books including Quran, tafsir, hadith, creed, fiqh, family and educational titles.

sources.name: İSAM Library

sources.name: Bibliothèque Nationale du Royaume du Maroc — Digital Collections

sources.category: Indian Arabic Persian Urdu manuscript collection

sources.name: ICCR Arabic Manuscripts
sources.notes: Official ICCR collection page exposes named Arabic manuscripts including Bukhari Sharif and other Islamic works with view/detail links.

sources.name: UniSZA e-Manuscript
sources.notes: Malaysia Ministry of Education assigned UniSZA to Islamic manuscript digitization; the repository includes collections from Terengganu, Aceh/Riau, Pattani, Brunei and Malay scholars in Saudi Arabia.

sources.name: UiTM Jawi Repository
sources.notes: UiTM describes this repository as a digital platform collecting Jawi materials across classical Islamic fields including turath, Quran, hadith and worship.

sources.name: National Library of Turkey Digital Library
sources.notes: Official Turkish National Library digital system contains catalogue metadata and high-resolution digital poses for manuscripts, periodicals and other materials; the catalogue supports language, script and collection filters.

sources.name: Turkey Manuscripts Institution E-Book Library
sources.notes: Official Manuscripts Institution e-book portal currently provides a digital catalogue of publications associated with the institution and manuscript heritage, including Islamic/Ottoman works.

sources.name: Islamic University of Madinah Manuscripts Platform
sources.notes: The Islamic University of Madinah launched an official electronic platform for original manuscripts in 2024. Access and copying rights vary by manuscript.

sources.name: Bangladesh Quran Digital
sources.notes: Current official portal exposes Arabic-English and Arabic-Bangla-English Quranic e-books and Quran audio. Useful for Bengali coverage; redistribution rights must be checked.

sources.name: Fawaz Quran API
sources.notes: Open-source repository aggregates 400+ Quran translations in 90+ languages. The repository is Unlicense, but individual translations retain their own provenance/rights requirements and some were OCRed; treat as discovery/structured-source and verify each edition.

sources.name: Ummah Library
sources.notes: Open-source Quran and Islamic knowledge platform; current README reports a runtime catalogue of about 490 translations across about 98 languages, with offline/API support. Underlying translation rights must be retained separately.

sources.name: Gaitco Quran Database
sources.notes: Structured Quran database with 134 translation/edition entries, SQLite/MySQL exports, provenance documentation and SHA-256 manifests. Useful for reproducible QA, but translation licenses remain edition-specific.

sources.name: Tafsir API — spa5k
sources.notes: Public repository exposes 122 Tafsir resources with multilingual support and several CDN/raw endpoints, and documents self-hosting. Underlying Tafsir texts remain subject to their respective source/licensing conditions.

sources.name: Bonyan API
sources.notes: Open-source unified API combining Quran, Tafsir, Azkar, Hadith and other Islamic utilities with multi-source fallback. Use for source discovery and integration; upstream rights/provenance must remain explicit.

sources.name: Asiatic Society of Bangladesh Library
sources.notes: The Asiatic Society of Bangladesh maintains a specialized research library of about 26,000 items including books, journals and manuscripts; access is regulated and copying services are provided under library rules.

sources.category: Bangladeshi and South Asian Islamic manuscripts
sources.name: Khulna/Bangladesh Manuscript Resources — ASB ecosystem
sources.notes: OPAC endpoint for searchable catalogue records. Treated as a bibliographic discovery endpoint rather than a direct redistribution source.

sources.name: National and University Library of Bosnia and Herzegovina — HMML
sources.notes: HMML collection page reports 1,047 preserved digital surrogates from the National and University Library of Bosnia and Herzegovina, in multiple Islamic and regional languages.

sources.name: Gazi Husrev-Bey Library Manuscript Fund
sources.notes: Official library page reports 10,585 manuscript codices containing about 16,907 works across Islamic sciences and related disciplines. Use as a collection/discovery source; digital copy rights vary by item.

sources.name: Bosniak Institute Oriental-Islamic Manuscripts
sources.notes: Institute reports 1,086 codices containing 1,662 works across theology, law, ethics, lexicography, history and other fields. Register as a manuscript discovery/reference lane; digitized-copy availability varies.

sources.name: Rampur Raza Library
sources.notes: Government of India describes the library as holding about 17,000 manuscripts in Arabic, Persian, Pashto, Sanskrit, Urdu, Hindi and Turkish, plus about 60,000 printed books. Digital access and reuse rights vary by item.

sources.category: Uzbekistan Islamic heritage and manuscript center
sources.name: Islamic Civilization Center in Uzbekistan
sources.notes: Official Center site documents a library and digital heritage work around ancient Islamic manuscripts, including the Uthman Quran and Central Asian collections. Actual digital-copy reuse rights must be checked per object.

sources.name: IRCICA Manuscript Collection — Open Access DSpace
sources.notes: IRCICA's open-access DSpace community contains 530 works under 284 titles focused on Islamic religion, history and literature, with continuing digitization and downloadable digital objects where provided.

sources.name: IRCICA Library and Archive
sources.notes: IRCICA library collection includes books, periodicals, manuscripts, rare books and audiovisual material in major Islamic languages plus Swahili and Zulu; digital transfer is ongoing.

sources.name: JAKIM Smart Quran
sources.notes: Official JAKIM page documents Smart Quran with Madinah Mushaf V2, Malay and English translations and named reciters. It is an app/source reference rather than a direct PDF repository.

sources.name: JAKIM Smart Hadith
sources.notes: Official JAKIM platform for hadith collections searchable by book, chapter and narrator. Useful as a Malaysian institutional hadith discovery lane; bulk reuse rights require verification.

sources.name: JAKIM myHadith Portal
sources.notes: Official JAKIM portal describes myHadith as an authoritative Malaysian gateway and central database for hadith research information.

sources.name: IRCICA — Catalogue of Turkic Manuscripts of Kazakhstan
sources.notes: 2026 IRCICA/Kazakhstan catalogue documents Turkic manuscripts held by the National Library of Kazakhstan alongside valuable Arabic and Persian manuscript holdings.

sources.name: Al-Azhar Digital Library
sources.notes: Current Al-Azhar digital library interface supports manuscripts, books, theses, research and journals with language filters. Useful as a primary institutional discovery lane; item-level download and redistribution terms apply.

sources.name: National Library of Tunisia — Manuscripts
sources.notes: Official National Library of Tunisia page reports about 24,000 manuscript volumes / roughly 43,000 titles across Arabic and Islamic culture, including Quran and hadith manuscripts, with a collection-wide indexing database.

sources.name: Bibliotheca Alexandrina Manuscript Museum — Digital Projects
sources.notes: Bibliotheca Alexandrina describes a project to create complete digital copies of its manuscript holdings and a 100,000-manuscript initiative collecting digital/microfilm copies from worldwide manuscript libraries, including Islamic manuscript collections.

sources.category: West African Arabic manuscript union catalogue
sources.name: West African Arabic Manuscript Database (WAAMD)
sources.notes: WAAMD is a bilingual union catalogue of West African Arabic manuscripts, covering collections in Mauritania, Mali, Ghana, Nigeria/Northwestern, Niger and related holdings in Europe/US. It is a discovery/catalogue layer rather than a blanket manuscript download source.

sources.name: HMML Islamic Manuscripts Repository List
sources.notes: HMML repository index lists institutions and collections where HMML has digitized Islamic manuscripts, spanning Africa, the Middle East, Asia and Europe. It is an important discovery layer for specific collection endpoints.

sources.name: Khalidi Library Jerusalem — HMML
sources.notes: HMML records 1,680 digital surrogates from the Khalidi Library, with extensive Hanafi-law and Islamic manuscript holdings. Useful for fiqh and Arabic/Persian/Ottoman research.

sources.name: Meyli Foundation Manuscript Collection — HMML
sources.notes: HMML records 265 complete digital surrogates from the Meyli Foundation collection, including Islamic theological, legal and spiritual works.

sources.name: Kantonalni Archive Travnik — HMML
sources.notes: HMML reports 120 digital surrogates from Travnik holdings, including Arabic, Persian and Ottoman Turkish manuscript and printed works.

sources.name: Sherif Harar City Museum — HMML
sources.notes: HMML reports 592 digital surrogates from Sherif Harar City Museum, primarily Islamic manuscripts on law, theology and devotional practice. Particularly useful for East African Arabic/Ajami language coverage.

sources.name: National Archives and Library of Ethiopia — HMML
sources.notes: HMML documents 174 digital/microform surrogates from the National Archives and Library of Ethiopia, with Arabic among the manuscript languages. This is a secondary discovery lane alongside the Islamic Sherif Harar collection.

sources.name: Private Collection of La Ode Zaenu — DREAMSEA / HMML
sources.notes: DREAMSEA/HMML collection in Southeast Sulawesi contains 124 digital surrogates of primarily Islamic texts including Quran commentary, hadith commentary, jurisprudence, prayer and theology, in Arabic/Malay/Javanese/Wolio scripts and traditions.

sources.name: Al-Jami al-Umari al-Kabir Gaza — HMML
sources.notes: HMML reports 211 digital surrogates from the Great Omari Mosque in Gaza, primarily Arabic works on Islamic law, theology and devotional practice.

sources.name: SAVAMA-DCI — Timbuktu Manuscripts on Google Arts & Culture
sources.notes: Google Arts & Culture presents the SAVAMA-DCI Timbuktu manuscript project and digitized heritage, including Islamic jurisprudence and Quran-related materials. It is an exhibit/discovery layer; follow the underlying holder and item rights for reuse.

sources.name: UAE General Authority for Islamic Affairs, Endowments and Zakat

sources.name: Qatar Ministry of Endowments — Islamic Books
sources.notes: Official Ministry catalogue contains Islamic books across fiqh, tafsir, creed and other fields, with full-text book pages and downloadable publication functions on item pages.

sources.name: Mushaf Qatar

sources.name: Sheikh Abdulla Bin Zaid Al Mahmoud Islamic Cultural Center Digital Library

sources.name: Kuwait Quran Affairs Department

sources.name: Kuwait Ministry of Awqaf — Research and Islamic Encyclopedias

sources.name: Algerian Ministry of Religious Affairs — Manuscripts
sources.notes: Official Algerian Ministry manuscript portal organizes manuscripts into Quran/علومه, Hadith/Seerah, Creed/Tawhid, Fiqh/Usul and other sections, with detailed manuscript records.

sources.name: Egypt Ministry of Awqaf — Central Library of Islamic Manuscripts
sources.notes: Official Egyptian Awqaf central Islamic manuscript library documents historic Quran and Islamic manuscripts held by the ministry.

sources.name: Jordan Ministry of Awqaf — Authorized Quran Editions
sources.notes: Official Jordan Awqaf Quran page provides authorized and unauthorized edition lists, useful for edition verification and provenance gating.

sources.name: Pakistan Ministry of Religious Affairs — Standard Copy of the Holy Quran

sources.name: Punjab Auqaf E-Library
sources.notes: Official Punjab Auqaf e-library exposes Al-Quran and digitized religious titles such as Zaad-ul-Matloob, Majalla Maarif-e-Auliya and other heritage works.

sources.name: National Centre for the Holy Quran (Maldives)
sources.notes: Government National Centre for the Holy Quran under Maldives Ministry of Islamic Affairs explicitly provides Quran, translations and other Islamic literature for free download in various formats/languages.

sources.name: Somalia Ministry of Endowments and Islamic Affairs — Audio

sources.name: Mauritania National Library

sources.name: Moroccan Muhammad VI Digital Quran

sources.notes: Official National Library page documents a dedicated manuscript room containing significant Mauritanian written heritage and research holdings.

sources.notes: Current Azerbaijan National Library digital reading interface exposes e-books and PDF downloads; collection-level rights are not blanket and must be checked per item.

sources.notes: Harvard states that its Islamic Heritage Project cataloged, conserved and digitized hundreds of Islamic manuscripts, maps and published texts and made these materials freely available online.

sources.name: Royal Danish Library — Oriental Collection

sources.name: ULB Bonn — Oriental Manuscripts

sources.name: McGill Islamic Studies Library Digital Collections

sources.name: McGill Islamic Studies Collection — Internet Archive
